blocks.label: ABOUT EAGLE RAY EXPEDITIONS
blocks.text: Private sailing in the Sea of Cortez, from La Paz. The boat is how we get there, and we choose it as carefully as the crew: catamarans and monohulls with all comforts, a flybridge, Starlink and everything for day & night in the water, from paddleboards to snorkel gear. What our clients take home are days at sea with their own people, and a crew chosen for how they sail and how they look after a guest. No unbreakable agenda, nothing for them to organise.
blocks.closing: The kind of trip they come back from and never forget.

blocks.title: Private sailing in the Sea of Cortez
blocks.text: Your own group, your own boat. The crew runs the sea, the day is yours: diving in, learning the wind, a kite session, a long lunch from the chef, or nothing at all.

blocks.title: Ocean adventures led by passionate sea people
blocks.text: We don’t hire crews. We choose people: passionate sea people who can’t stay away from the water, who notice before you ask, and who know when a group needs a dive or a nap. Everything that Eagle Ray is starts with them.

people.name: Lou
people.text: 15 years sailing the world, from the Bahamas to Polynesia. Master 200 GT captain and certified marine engineer: he has skippered catamarans from 41 to 62 feet and knows the boat from the helm to the engine room.
people.quote: "I read the sea and the group, and adjust the day as it goes. If it's your first time at sea, you're in the right place."

people.alt: Monik Saab Expedition Leader Eagle Ray
people.name: Monik
people.text: Dive instructor who guides in four languages, with six years in Baja. Licensed to guide in the Revillagigedo Islands, she has also worked on yachts with helicopter decks.
people.quote: "From the start, I watch the group's energy and how each person feels, and I adapt the way I lead to you."

people.name: Sergio
people.text: Survivor México champion and Ironman. He has led groups through Iceland, Hawaii and Guatemala's volcanoes, and guides freediving, spearfishing and open water swimming.
people.quote: "From the first moment, I watch how each person arrives. If someone needs to slow down, we slow down."

people.name: Juan Carlos
people.text: Dive instructor at 21, now a PADI Master Scuba Diver Trainer and TDI cave diver. He has taught in the Maldives and Indonesia, spent 30 days straight on a liveaboard to the Socorro Islands, and most recently sailed solo from Loreto to La Paz.
people.quote: "I start every trip with questions: what's your name, have you been in these waters before, what do you definitely want to live? Then I plan around your answers."

people.alt: Andrea Gutiérrez Ramírez, Eagle Ray Expeditions
people.name: Andrea
people.text: She crossed the Atlantic in a rowing boat. Five years guiding groups at sea in Mexico, with STCW and RYA safety training.
people.quote: "On day one, I watch how each person arrives: their energy, their confidence. My job is to show you what you're capable of, without unnecessary risks."
